provenance.decision: OWNER 2026-08-11: 'colour theme and branding must freez as we have in website'. The WEBSITE is canonical and FROZEN for brand colour. The platform moves to it. Where the two disagree, the website's value wins.
provenance.dark: crowagent-website/astro/src/styles/tokens.css - the V6 hue shelf and ground ladder, which is what crowagent.ai actually serves.
provenance.light: crowagent-website/concepts/platform-theme/theme.css [data-mode='light'] - the website-authored, contrast-measured light column for the platform (contrast.mjs / ratios.json in that directory, zero failures).
provenance.note: The astro dark ladder is one revision NEWER than the concept's dark column (floor 02040A vs 03040A, canvas 050814 vs 05070E, panel 0B1024 vs 0C1020). The shipping astro values win. Every one of the three is DARKER than the concept's, so every contrast ratio the concept measured against light ink improves rather than regresses.

voidedAudit.what: The platform UI/UX audit brief section 3 names rgb(4,14,26) (#040E1A) as the foundation to preserve.
voidedAudit.status: VOID ON COLOUR - owner 2026-08-11. That audit ran against the platform's CURRENT theme with a tool that had no knowledge of the brand change, so it DESCRIBES the defect rather than stating the target. #040E1A is not a preserve-target.

light.why: NOT the website's derived light teal #0F766E. Platform --teal in light is a FILL that carries --on-accent (#04121E) as its label: #04121E on #0F766E measures 3.43:1 and fails WCAG AA, where #04121E on #0A9A80 measures 5.4:1. #0F766E is teal-as-INK and only becomes correct once the V6 control-neutrality work lands (ADOPTION.md A4/A5), which is a separate programme. Light is NOT flattened onto the dark value.

brand-teal-deep.role: the teal hover / pressed step. Platform --teal-d.

light.why: measured 5.22:1 against --bg (DYN-A11Y-03). Follows brand-teal, which is platform-held in light for the reason above.

ground-3.role: elevated / inset wells and tracks. Platform --surf2.

ground-4.role: deepest inset / pressed / row-hover. Platform --surf3 AND --surf4, which collapse.

ink-2.role: muted secondary / tertiary text. Platform --mist AND --dim-c, which collapse.

ladderNotes.surfaces: Six platform ground steps map onto five website ones; --surf3 and --surf4 collapse onto ground-4. That collapse is the website's own finding, not a choice made here (concepts/platform-theme/README.md section 3, 'Six platform steps to five website ones; --surf3 and --surf4 collapse'). Assignment is by LIGHTNESS ORDER within each mode, which is why the website token a slot draws from differs between modes: the light ladder is not a mirror of the dark one (light --c-raised is already #FFFFFF, so light lights DOWNWARD as a surface recedes). Monotonicity is preserved in both modes, so no existing elevation relationship inverts.
ladderNotes.surfacesLightExtraCollapse: The light column offers only FOUR distinct grounds (#FFFFFF, #F5F6FA, #EDF0F7, #E7EAF2), so in light --bg-deep, --surf3 and --surf4 all land on ground-4/#E7EAF2. Three tokens on one value. This is a property of the source, not an invention.
ladderNotes.ink: Four platform ink steps map onto three website ones; --mist and --dim-c collapse onto ink-2. The website's own mapping table names --steel/--mist as the merging pair on nearest-VALUE grounds; this file merges --mist/--dim-c instead, on ROLE grounds, because the platform documents --steel and --mist as deliberately non-interchangeable (R24-UIDE-004) and --dim-c is the tertiary step that has no website counterpart. Dark --dim-c #7E96B0 -> #A9B6D2 and light #6B7688 -> #5A6478 both INCREASE contrast against their own ground.

unreconciled.reason: RULE 0-C: never invent, guess or estimate a brand value. The website palette contains no counterpart for these, so they are NAMED here rather than derived.

tokens.--teal-l: #6EE9D2 - lighter teal step. No website counterpart.
tokens.--line-deep: #1E3A58 - navy rule. No website counterpart; still on the OLD navy family.
tokens.--bg-tint: #04101A - tinted page wash. No website counterpart; still on the OLD navy family.
tokens.--sky/--gold/--core/--nest/--sight/--tra: the website palette has two hues and two markers and no home for these eight accents (concepts/platform-theme/README.md section 3).
tokens.--err/--warn/--success/--coral: the website palette carries no red and no green. The concept derives --p-danger #FF7A85 dark / #B32131 light but binding it is the role-layer programme, not a value swap.
tokens.light --border/--scrim-modal: declared as rgba(10, 31, 58, a) in the light block - channels taken from the OLD dark --surf. Left as found; no website counterpart for a light scrim.
tokens.light --ca-teal-text: #0A6E5C - the light-canvas teal INK / rescue FILL. Platform-held, no website counterpart, so only its DARK value is bound (to brand-teal, blocks root+dark). It is a THIRD light teal on purpose and not redundancy: --teal #0A9A80 is the resting fill (5.36:1 under an obsidian label), --teal-d #077663 is the hover/pressed STEP, and this is the value the DYN-A11Y-01/02/04/05 rescue rules pin when a teal fill has to carry a WHITE label or teal has to act as ink. Collapsing it onto --teal-d would clear every floor (5.55:1 both ways vs 6.18/5.97) but would make a rescued control stop changing colour on hover - the same defect the Word task pane shipped. MEASURED 2026-08-11 against the frozen light grounds: as ink 5.97:1 on #FFFFFF, 5.14:1 on the deepest ground #E7EAF2, 5.45:1 on the --teal-dim wash; as fill under white 6.18:1. [CLOSED 2026-08-11] Seven consuming declarations in web/app/globals.css and apps/portal/src/app/globals.css re-typed this hex instead of reading the token that already held it; they now read var(--ca-teal-text).
tokens.light --ca-fg-muted (CLOSED 2026-08-11): WAS UNBOUND IN LIGHT and had duly drifted. It was declared `#586577` with the comment '= light --mist', but the freeze moved light --mist to #5A6478, so the alias and the token it claims to mirror held DIFFERENT values while every drift guard stayed green; an unbound key is invisible to the guard, which is the same shape as the LIGHT_THEME_TOKENS finding recorded in platformConstantBindings._lightGroupNote. It is a branding defect rather than a contrast one: #586577 measured 5.20:1 on light --surf2 against #5A6478's 5.22:1, so nothing was failing. Bound to ink-2 in all three blocks now, which is what --mist, --dim-c and --ca-fg-disabled already were.
tokens.--teal-40 / --teal-45 in the dark block: MEASURED ABSENT: unlike their eleven --teal-NN siblings these two are declared only at :root and are NOT re-asserted in [data-theme="dark"]. Bound at root only, because this generator never inserts a declaration. Harmless today (:root IS the dark palette) but it is the same shape as the light-OS freeze defect the tokens suite guards elsewhere, and it is recorded here rather than silently patched.

neverTouch.--mark: #A78BFA CrowMark product identity. Already byte-identical to the website's --c-violet.

platformBindings._templateSyntax: {hex:PIGMENT} -> #RRGGBB ; {rgb:PIGMENT} -> 'r, g, b'. A binding is applied ONLY to blocks listed in `blocks` AND only where the declaration already exists - the generator never inserts a token.
platformBindings._rootUses: The :root block holds the DARK palette (color-scheme: dark). Bindings listing 'root' therefore resolve against the pigment's DARK value; 'light'/'dark' resolve against their own.

platformConstantBindings._why: constants.ts is a TypeScript MIRROR of the same palette, for consumers that cannot read a CSS custom property: Chart.js (canvas), the email templates, the PDF/DOCX/OG generators. A hand-maintained mirror is the same RULE 0-C defect as an independent website palette, one file closer in. MEASURED, 2026-08-11, before this pass touched anything: BRAND_COLOR_TOKENS.teal and CA_ALIAS_TOKENS.teal held #33D9BD while tokens.css held #0CC9A8, and TEXT_SCALE_TOKENS.dimC held #7A9AAE while tokens.css held #7E96B0. The mirror had ALREADY drifted from the file it mirrors, in three places, with nothing failing. It is generated from here now.
platformConstantBindings._note: These consumers are dark-only today (CHART_COLOURS carries a header saying so). Every binding resolves against the pigment's DARK value.
platformConstantBindings._lightGroupNote: LIGHT_THEME_TOKENS is the PRINT / light canvas the PDF, DOCX and XLSX generators paint on, and it is the ONE colour group in constants.ts that is not dark. Bound with the @light mode suffix. MEASURED 2026-08-11, before these bindings existed: ten of its twelve colour keys disagreed with the reconciled [data-theme="light"] block in tokens.css that they cite in their own comments (bg #F6F8FB vs #F5F6FA, bgDeep #EEF2F7 vs #E7EAF2, surf2 #F2F5F9 vs #EDF0F7, surf3 #E9EEF5 vs #E7EAF2, surf4 #DFE6F0 vs #E7EAF2, cloud #14181F vs #0B0E19, steel #3A4655 vs #2B3245, mist #586577 vs #5A6478, dimC #6B7688 vs #5A6478). Only teal/tealD already agreed. An UNBOUND key is invisible to the drift guard, so this group drifted silently while every bound key was green. gridPrint, inkPrint, ragRed, ragGreen, ragRedTint, ragAmberTint and coralPrint are deliberately NOT bound: brand.source.json records no counterpart for them, they ship on customer documents today, and inventing one would breach RULE 0-C. They are named here so their absence is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.
